summary: For khanom khai (small baked egg cakes), Tourism Authority of Thailand recommends Ua Chang Seng in Chiang Mai’s Chang Moi/Kad Luang food district. The bakery also sells other traditional Chinese-style sweets, making it an easy takeaway stop alongside Warorot Market.
whyGo: Try a local old-style egg cake at the specific shop highlighted by TAT for this dessert.
Browse other traditional sweets and watch for fresh batches, then continue on foot to Warorot Market and nearby Ton Lam Yai.
bestFor: Travelers who enjoy small, inexpensive local sweets and takeaway bakery stops.
A short food detour while exploring the Chang Moi and Kad Luang market district.
skipIf: You avoid eggs or wheat; the signature cake is egg-based and ingredient handling or cross-contact is not documented.
You need a sit-down dessert venue or guaranteed step-free access; sources describe this mainly as a bakery/takeaway stop and access is undocumented.
duration: Allow 10–20 minutes to buy and sample sweets; combine with the market district for a longer visit. These are planning estimates.
cost: Wongnai currently shows the dessert price band and recent reviews report khanom khai at about ฿45 per bag, with some other sweets at ฿15 each. Treat these as indicative, not a guaranteed December 2026 menu price; bring small cash.
hours: Wongnai listed the shop as open until 19:30 when checked. A complete, reliable weekly schedule was not available; confirm close to the visit, particularly around holidays.
bestTime: Go during the listed daytime-to-early-evening window and ask whether a fresh batch is available. TAT situates the stop in an evening sweets itinerary, but current daily baking times are unconfirmed.
gettingThere: Ua Chang Seng is at 36/3 Chang Moi Tat Mai Road, Chang Moi, opposite Wat Nam Tharee/Wat Khaek in the Warorot Market area. Ask for “Ue Chang Seng” or show the Thai name อื้อชั่งเซ้ง. From nearby Kad Luang/Warorot, walk; from elsewhere in central Chiang Mai, use a local songthaew, tuk-tuk or ride-hail. Parking is limited street parking according to a recent customer review, so walking or a drop-off is more practical.
booking: No booking is indicated; this is a bakery counter. Walk in and buy while stock is available. Call numbers shown on Wongnai (053-232-268 or 053-413-125) to check stock or hours, though connection and English support are not confirmed.
accessibility: No formal accessibility information was found. The listing and recent review describe a street-front shop and takeaway; step-free entrance, counter height, seating and accessible toilet are unconfirmed. The surrounding market streets can be busy.
practicalTips: Khanom khai is an egg cake; ask staff about ingredients if you have allergies or dietary restrictions. Wheat, dairy and cross-contact details are not published.
Khanom khai and khanom khai hong are different sweets; show the Thai shop name and ask for ขนมไข่ if needed.
The bakery sells multiple sweets, so ask the price before ordering and whether items are sold by bag or piece.
Pair the stop with Warorot Market; TAT also points to dessert vendors at the adjacent Ton Lam Yai market.
decemberNotes: A convenient indoor/outdoor food-district stop for a December Chiang Mai day or early evening. No December 2026 special hours or event were found; year-end holiday trading may differ, so check directly before making a dedicated trip. Crowded market streets and traffic are possible around holiday periods.
uncertainties: The TAT recommendation dates to 2020; the business listing currently identifies Ua Chang Seng at its Chang Moi address, but independent confirmation of December 2026 operation is unavailable.
Hours are shown as a current closing-time indicator rather than a verified weekly schedule, and baked-item stock varies.
Menu prices are based on a current listing and customer reviews, not a published official price list; ingredients beyond egg and allergy controls are not confirmed.
Accessibility and December 2026 holiday hours are not documented.
